candidates.explanation: The application operation, provider port, SSE lifecycle, abort/idle-timeout handling, commit-aware failures, job semantics, redaction, and provider isolation are coherent. However, assistant behavior is dispersed across domain, ports, use-cases, adapters, boundary, and infrastructure roots rather than colocated under one capability root.

The proposal clearly defines a framework-neutral operation and provider port, correctly handles cancellation, inactivity timeout, pre/post-commit failures, native HTTP/job outcomes, safe reporting, and provider isolation. Its capability files are nevertheless distributed across many layer-oriented roots rather than one assistant capability root.

The design provides the required neutral use case, abort-aware provider seam, SSE Route Handler, idle watchdog, commit-sensitive failure protocol, single reporting guard, and job retry/dead-letter flow without provider leakage. Assistant behavior is spread among application, providers, transport, jobs, and infrastructure roots, so colocation is missing.

The assistant capability is coherently colocated under src/modules/assistant with a justified Route Handler entrypoint. It cleanly separates the neutral generation operation and provider port from SSE and job-native contracts, propagates cancellation, implements an idle-only timeout, changes failure representation after commitment, reports unexpected failures once, and prevents provider details or SDK types from escaping.
